title: Build an ambient fish tank screen with AI help
summary: A backend developer spent 50-70 hours building a pixel-art fish tank for a kitchen screen, using AI models for code, art direction and even fish-swimming research.
agent_role: The AI model helped design systems, write game code and find research papers on fish swimming patterns to base the movement on; the author directed the art and design.
outcome: Author reports a finished fish tank simulation now running on a 24-inch kitchen screen, built in 50-70 hours with no prior game development experience.
what_they_did: A backend developer with no game-making experience built a calm fish tank animation to run on a 24-inch screen in his kitchen, powered by a small used PC. He leaned on AI models throughout: writing code, shaping the look, and at one point finding research papers on how fish swim so the movement could be based on them. He also added a birthday surprise: three fish carrying codes that led his wife to real-world quests.
how_it_went: He says the project took about 50 to 70 hours over several months, and the tank now replaces a photo slideshow on the kitchen screen.
worth_knowing: He had to swap a small Raspberry Pi for a used mini PC with a better graphics chip to run the animation smoothly.
prompt: Help me build an ambient animated scene I can leave running on a screen at home, themed around [your theme]. Work with me step by step: first propose a simple design and the technology to use, then write the code in small pieces I can run and check. Research how [the creatures or objects] really move and behave, cite your sources, and base the animation on that. Keep it lightweight enough to run on [your device]. Show me a plan before writing any code, and pause for my feedback after each stage.

curation.rationale: A real personal project built over months with heavy help from AI models, including having the model find fish-swimming research and turn it into code, but the agent's exact role is only loosely described.
